result:
I changed nothing this run. The CPU limit is the bottleneck: 8 FEBio runs are using about 27 of our 32 cores. Nothing is hung and all services are up.

- **Runs:** 8 running (4 on GPU, 4 on CPU) and 7 waiting since 09:58. Every run log was written to in the last 16 s. One run (p073) finished in the last hour, taking 32 min on GPU; the CPU runs started at 16:59 and are still going.
- **Why I didn't add runs:** GPU4 is empty and my GPU runs sit at 0–53 % load, but each GPU run also takes 4 CPU cores. Raising the limit to 1.5× before left the runs 90 % throttled, so more runs would not finish faster.
- **Memory:** 124.7 of 128 GiB, but only 60 GiB is held by processes. The other 65 GiB is file cache that can be reclaimed, and the scheduler keeps its 16 GB buffer. No new out-of-memory kills.
- **Other queue:** the newer repo's task queue is empty (1 done, 5 old gate2 failures, unchanged).
- **Disk:** /raid has 38 GB free (56 GB at 16:54). The 7 waiting runs need about 19 GB more on top of what the running ones still write. That should stay above the 15 GB floor, but it is close. If it drops below 15 GB, the next check pauses new launches.
- **Restart coverage:** all long jobs are covered. The two prerun sessions in `ops/resume_all.sh` are correctly not running because their jobs are already marked done.

**Needs a person:** more free space on /raid, so launches don't have to be paused again.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261030_1754.md
- status.json

I also added one line to `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
